unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

chapter: v3 · The Nome King
unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

label: v4 · CHAPTER 18. ContentsTHE TRIAL OF EUREKA THE KITTEN
value: One of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room.
chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 18. ContentsTHE TRIAL OF EUREKA THE KITTEN
unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

chapter: v1 · Chapter XX The Dainty China Country
unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

chapter: v1 · Chapter V The Rescue of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy and the Scarecrow wake up and discover the Tin Woodman, rusted motionless in the forest. After Dorothy oils his joints, he joins their journey to the Emerald City in hopes of getting a heart from Oz. As they continue along the yellow brick road, the Tin Woodman recounts how the Wicked Witch of the East cursed his axe, leading to his tin transformation and loss of his heart.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions travel through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft, but the swift current sweeps them off course and leaves the Scarecrow stuck on a pole. Continuing their journey through a field of deadly scarlet poppies, Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion succumb to the flowers' magical sleeping spell, forcing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to carry Dorothy and Toto to safety while leaving the heavy Lion behind.

unit: The Tin Woodman slays a wildcat that is chasing the Queen of the Field Mice, earning her gratitude and the assistance of her subjects. unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

value: Dorothy uses Ozma's magic picture.
chapter: v3 · Dorothy's Magic Belt
unit: Dorothy uses Ozma's magic picture to check on Aunt Em and Uncle Henry, seeing that Uncle Henry is sick and lonely in Australia. Seeking a way to join him without losing the magic belt, Dorothy and Ozma consult Glinda, who suggests Ozma wear the belt and wish Dorothy to Australia. After saying farewell to all her friends in Oz, Dorothy is magically transported to Australia to care for Uncle Henry.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. After accidentally startling a milkmaid and causing her cow to break a leg, they speak with a china princess and a cracked clown named Mr. Joker, who explain how fragile they are and why they cannot leave their land. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 1. ContentsTHE EARTHQUAKE
unit: Dorothy arrives at Hugson's Siding after a late train ride delayed by earthquakes. She meets Zeb and his horse Jim, who are driving her in a buggy to Hugson's Ranch. value: Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim float down through a subterranean chasm.
chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 2. ContentsTHE GLASS CITY
unit: Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim float down through a subterranean chasm illuminated by six colored suns. The horse Jim and Dorothy's kitten Eureka both gain the ability to speak, and they gently land on the roof of a glass house in an underground city. Discovering they can walk on air, the group steps down to the street where they are met by a crowd of serene, expressionless people, one of whom asks if they caused the recent earthquake.

value: Dorothy and Zeb meet Gwig the Sorcerer in the glass palace.
chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 3. ContentsTHE ARRIVAL OF THE WIZARD
unit: In the glass palace, Dorothy and Zeb meet Gwig the Sorcerer, who accuses them of causing the earthquake damage before a descending balloon draws everyone outside. The balloon lands, revealing the Wizard of Oz, who explains his fall into the earth and is invited to compete against Gwig. After performing magic tricks with piglets to prove his superiority, the Wizard uses a sword to slice Gwig in half when the Sorcerer attempts to stop his breath, discovering that the Mangaboos are vegetable beings.

unit: The Princess of the Mangaboos announces that the human visitors and their animals will be destroyed unless the Wizard can prove his sorcery. Later, while the Wizard sleeps, the Mangaboos corner Jim, Eureka, and the nine piglets and force them out of the city toward the mountain pit despite a fierce fight from the horse and kitten.

chapter: v2 · The Transformation of Old Mombi
unit: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi in disguise. Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

Once Jellia reveals that everyone in Oz speaks the same language, the Scarecrow and Jack clear up the confusion and agree to become friends.

label: v2 · The Scarecrow Plans an escape
value: Tip follows the Soldier to the palace.
chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Plans an escape
unit: Tip follows the Soldier to the palace, where the Scarecrow learns that the Emerald City is being conquered by an army of girls. After taking time to reflect, the Scarecrow decides to escape on the Sawhorse to seek help from the Tin Woodman. Tied securely together on the wooden horse, Tip, Jack, and the Scarecrow burst through the palace gates and out of the city, only to plunge into a wide river at full speed.

value: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman.
chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. unit: While traveling, the Woggle-Bug annoys the group with puns until the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman tell him to restrain himself. Led safely by the Mouse Queen, the travelers overcome the magical obstacles and arrive outside the Emerald City.

unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. Jinjur signals her Army of Revolt to ambush and disarm the group, threatening them with execution. The Scarecrow releases mice hidden in his straw, causing the female rebels and Jinjur to flee in panic, allowing the group to secure the palace doors.

chapter: v2 · The Astonishing Flight of the Gump
unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

value: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip
chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

value: General Jinjur summons Mombi.
chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

chapter: v2 · A Highly Magnified History
unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. He accepts an invitation from Tip and the group to join them on their journey to the Emerald City. When the issue of the Saw-Horse's broken leg arises, the Woggle-Bug suggests using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs to fix it, allowing the party to resume their travel.

unit: While traveling, the Woggle-Bug annoys the group with puns until the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman tell him to restrain himself. unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. value: The group gathers various odd items on the roof.
chapter: v2 · The Astonishing Flight of the Gump
unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

label: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
value: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip
chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. Jinjur signals her Army of Revolt to ambush and disarm the group, threatening them with execution. The Scarecrow releases mice hidden in his straw, causing the female rebels and Jinjur to flee in panic, allowing the group to secure the palace doors.

label: v2 · The Scarecrow Takes Time to Think
value: The group is trapped inside the palace by Jinjur's army.
chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Takes Time to Think
unit: Trapped inside the palace by Jinjur's army, the group despairs over their situation until the Scarecrow devises a plan to escape by air. Tip reveals he has one last dose of the Powder of Life, so the Scarecrow suggests building a flying machine on the roof and bringing it to life. After Nick Chopper fixes Jack Pumpkinhead's leg with a wooden table leg, the companions set out to search the palace for materials.

chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 15. ContentsOLD FRIENDS ARE REUNITED
unit: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb, and Jim is given a room inside the palace. Zeb gets dressed in fine Oz clothing before attending a dinner with Dorothy, Ozma, and the Wizard, where the Wizard explains his origins and history in Oz. chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 6. ContentsTHE MANGABOOS PROVE DANGEROUS
unit: The Princess of the Mangaboos announces that the human visitors and their animals will be destroyed unless the Wizard can prove his sorcery. The Wizard uses lit lanterns and burning kerosene oil to impress the Princess and scorch her bad advisors, convincing her to spare the humans while insisting the animals still be sent to the Black Pit. Later, while the Wizard sleeps, the Mangaboos corner Jim, Eureka, and the nine piglets and force them out of the city toward the mountain pit despite a fierce fight from the horse and kitten.

chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 18. ContentsTHE TRIAL OF EUREKA THE KITTEN
unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

unit: Glinda's army arrives and surrounds the Emerald City, demanding that Queen Jinjur hand over Mombi. Mombi uses magic to disguise Jellia Jamb as herself, but Glinda sees through the trick and demands the real witch. When Glinda's forces enter the city to search, Mombi transforms into a red rose, which the Tin Woodman plucks and unwittingly carries out of the city into Glinda's camp.

value: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi.
chapter: v2 · The Transformation of Old Mombi
unit: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi in disguise. Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

label: v2 · The Riches of Content
value: General Jinjur refuses to step down.
chapter: v2 · The Riches of Content
unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

value: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin.
chapter: v2 · A Highly Magnified History
unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. He accepts an invitation from Tip and the group to join them on their journey to the Emerald City. When the issue of the Saw-Horse's broken leg arises, the Woggle-Bug suggests using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs to fix it, allowing the party to resume their travel.

unit: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi in disguise. Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

label: v3 · The Eleven Guesses

chapter: v3 · The Eleven Guesses
unit: Ozma accepts the Nome King's terms and enters his palace to try to guess which ornaments are the transformed royal family of Ev. The Nome King returns to announce her failure, prompting the Tin Woodman to step forward as the next person to enter the palace.

unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

chapter: v3 · The Nome King
unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

value: Billina repeatedly breaks the Nome King's enchantments.
chapter: v3 · The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
unit: As Billina repeatedly breaks the Nome King's enchantments, the angry King calls his warriors and tries to capture Dorothy, but the Sawhorse, Lion, and Tiger defend her. When the restored captives emerge, the King declares them prisoners, leading to a brief battle where the Scarecrow throws Billina's eggs at the King. Terrified by the eggs, the Nome army flees in panic, leaving the blinded King helpless as Billina tells Dorothy to seize his magical belt.

label: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

value: One of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room.
chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 18. ContentsTHE TRIAL OF EUREKA THE KITTEN
unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

unit: The Nome King watches with amusement as Ozma's officers and army attempt to guess the transformations, only for all of them to fail and become ornaments in his palace. label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

value: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
unit: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft, but the swift current sweeps them off course and leaves the Scarecrow stuck on a pole. Continuing their journey through a field of deadly scarlet poppies, Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion succumb to the flowers' magical sleeping spell, forcing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to carry Dorothy and Toto to safety while leaving the heavy Lion behind.

unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

value: Dorothy and her companions travel through a thick forest.

unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. label: Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

section: Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
label: Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

value: A young boy named Tip lives in the Gillikin region of Oz.
chapter: The Marvelous Powder of Life
unit: In the Gillikin region of Oz, a young boy named Tip lives under the care of the old sorceress Mombi, whom he dislikes. While Mombi is away on a two-day trip, Tip decides to construct a wooden figure with a carved pumpkin head to prank and frighten her. He completes the wooden dummy, dresses it in old clothes from Mombi's chest, and names his creation Jack Pumpkinhead.

value: Tip fears Mombi will turn him into a marble statue.
chapter: Tip Makes an Experiment in Magic
unit: Fearing Mombi will turn him into a marble statue, Tip decides to run away and steals the Powder of Life and some food. He retrieves Jack Pumpkinhead from the stable, and together they escape into the night. As they travel south toward the Emerald City, Tip explains the history and geography of Oz to Jack, including the ruler of the Emerald City, the Scarecrow.

chapter: Jack Pumpkinhead’s Ride to the Emerald City

label: His Majesty the Scarecrow

chapter: His Majesty the Scarecrow
unit: Tip, Jack, and the Saw-Horse cross a wide river by swimming across. label: The Journey to the Tin Woodman
value: Tip follows the Soldier to the palace.
chapter: The Journey to the Tin Woodman
unit: Tip follows the Soldier to the palace, where the Scarecrow learns that the Emerald City is being conquered by an army of girls. entity: General Jinjur, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Mombi, Horse, Jack Pumpkinhead, Bug
label: A Highly Magnified History
value: General Jinjur summons Mombi.
chapter: A Highly Magnified History
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

label: Old Mombi indulges in Witchcraft
value: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin.
chapter: Old Mombi indulges in Witchcraft
unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. He accepts an invitation from Tip and the group to join them on their journey to the Emerald City. When the issue of the Saw-Horse's broken leg arises, the Woggle-Bug suggests using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs to fix it, allowing the party to resume their travel.

label: The Prisoners of the Queen
value: The Woggle-Bug annoys the group with puns.
chapter: The Prisoners of the Queen
unit: While traveling, the Woggle-Bug annoys the group with puns until the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman tell him to restrain himself. The party encounters the Queen of the Field Mice, who lends twelve mice to hide in the Scarecrow's straw and guides them past several of Mombi's illusions. Led safely by the Mouse Queen, the travelers overcome the magical obstacles and arrive outside the Emerald City.

value: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City.
chapter: The Scarecrow Takes Time to Think
unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. Jinjur signals her Army of Revolt to ambush and disarm the group, threatening them with execution. The Scarecrow releases mice hidden in his straw, causing the female rebels and Jinjur to flee in panic, allowing the group to secure the palace doors.

section: The Astonishing Flight of the Gump
label: The Astonishing Flight of the Gump
value: The group is trapped inside the palace by Jinjur's army.
chapter: The Astonishing Flight of the Gump
unit: Trapped inside the palace by Jinjur's army, the group despairs over their situation until the Scarecrow devises a plan to escape by air. Tip reveals he has one last dose of the Powder of Life, so the Scarecrow suggests building a flying machine on the roof and bringing it to life. After Nick Chopper fixes Jack Pumpkinhead's leg with a wooden table leg, the companions set out to search the palace for materials.

Tip reveals he has one last dose of the Powder of Life, so the Scarecrow suggests building a flying machine on the roof and bringing it to life. After Nick Chopper fixes Jack Pumpkinhead's leg with a wooden table leg, the companions set out to search the palace for materials.

entity: Bug, Gump, Horse, Jack Pumpkinhead, Mombi, Nick Chopper, Scarecrow
label: In the Jackdaw’s Nest
value: The group gathers various odd items on the roof.
chapter: In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

chapter: The Yellow Hen
unit: A fierce storm strikes the ship carrying Dorothy and Uncle Henry on their way to Australia. Fearing her frail uncle has gone on deck in danger, Dorothy goes outside to find him, only to be blown overboard while holding onto a wooden chicken coop. Swept away into the sea, she manages to use the floating coop as a raft and eventually falls asleep once the storm subsides.

unit: The procession pauses so Billina can lay her daily egg, which the Scarecrow collects. unit: In the glass palace, Dorothy and Zeb meet Gwig the Sorcerer, who accuses them of causing the earthquake damage before a descending balloon draws everyone outside. The balloon lands, revealing the Wizard of Oz, who explains his fall into the earth and is invited to compete against Gwig. After performing magic tricks with piglets to prove his superiority, the Wizard uses a sword to slice Gwig in half when the Sorcerer attempts to stop his breath, discovering that the Mangaboos are vegetable beings.

chapter: CHAPTER 11. ContentsTHEY MEET THE WOODEN GARGOYLES
unit: The group ascends the stairs inside Pyramid Mountain, pausing at an opening to observe the surrounding sky, clouds, and black sea. Halfway up, they meet an eccentric braided man in a cavern who manufactures rustles and flutters. After trading a blue ribbon for his inventions and listening to his strange backstory, they bid him farewell and continue their climb.

unit: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb, and Jim is given a room inside the palace. Princess Ozma offers the Wizard a permanent home as Official Wizard, and several of Dorothy's old friends—including the Scarecrow, Billina, Eureka, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug—arrive to reunite with them.

The jury initially finds Eureka guilty, but the Tin Woodman interrupts the execution by producing a piglet from his hat. However, Eureka points out that the piglet lacks an emerald collar, prompting her to finally reveal that the real piglet is trapped inside a narrow vase in Ozma's room.
